plate_findings.evidence: Brain MRI demonstrated diffuse white matter signal abnormalities

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Brain MRI showing white matter signal abnormalities and bilateral globus pallidus involvement, consistent with metabolic storage disorder and later confirmed as fucosidosis via genetic and enzyme testing. B: Thoracolumbar MRI demonstrating classic skeletal changes (hypoplastic vertebral bodies with anterior beaking), which are consistent with severe forms of fucosidosis. C: Head CT confirming persistent hypodensities in the periventricular white matter, consistent with white matter involvement in a patient with confirmed fucosidosis.
panels.attribution_text: Wang and Xing. Case Report: A rare case of fucosidosis caused by a novel homozygous pathogenic variant in the FUCA1 gene within a 17.2 Mb region of homozygosity.. Frontiers in medicine 2026. doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1573922. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Brain MRI demonstrated diffuse white matter signal abnormalities and bilateral globus pallidus involvement, suggestive of a metabolic disorder such as leukodystrophy or mucopolysaccharidosis; (B) thoracolumbar MRI revealed hypoplastic vertebral bodies with anterior beaking and mild kyphosis, features commonly associated with severe forms of MPS; (C) CT imaging study of the head confirmed persistent hypodensities in the periventricular white matter and bilateral globus pallidus, consistent with leukodystrophy.
in_text_mentions: ain MRI demonstrated diffuse white matter signal abnormalities and bilateral globus pallidus involvement, suggestive of a metabolic disorder such as leukodystrophy or mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS) (see Figure 1A). A thoracolumbar MRI revealed hypoplastic vertebral bodies with anterior beaking and mild kyphosis, features commonly associated with severe forms of MPS (see Figure 1B). An EEG demonstrated nonspecific findings of cerebral dysfunction without evidence of seizure activity. Despite these findings, MPS enzyme and urine screening results were unremarkable, ruling out common lysosomal stora

Further CT imaging study of the head confirmed persistent hypodensities in the periventricular white matter and bilateral globus pallidus, consistent with leukodystrophy (see Figure 1C). Viral studies revealed HSV-1 infection, and the patient was treated with intravenous acyclovir. A leukodystrophy genetic panel identified a homozygous pathogenic variant c.557T>A (p.Leu186*) in the FUCA1 gene, which is located in the previously identified ROH. Further lysosomal enzyme testing using a whole blood panel confirmed the diagnostic impression, revealing a complete absence of α-L-fucosidase activity

in_text_mentions: dder, speech delay, fever, oral blisters, and cold extremities. A genetics consult was requested. During his time in Mexico, the patient had frequent hospitalizations for respiratory infections. Developmentally, he crawled at 16 months but lost this ability by age six. His hand clamping regressed into finger contractures, and leg stiffness worsened. Exam revealed coarse facial features, thick eyebrows, high nasal bridge, oral blisters, micrognathia (Figure 2A), muscular atrophy, abnormal lower limb posture secondary to hypertonia (Figure 2B), and red-purple, pinhead-sized papules on the trunk.
